policy_name: Artificial Intelligence (AI) IT Security and Information Governance Policy
issuing_authority: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (approved by the Trust Risk & Assurance Committee; owner: Senior Information Risk Owner)
country_region: United Kingdom (England) – Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London
regulatory_regime: NHS trust internal information security and information governance policy (under UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018, NIS Regulations and the NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit)
geo_constraints: All sites of Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust; staff, contractors and third parties accessing Trust information systems

locale_context.region: Europe › United Kingdom (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
locale_context.regulation: Internal policy · information security and information governance controls for AI
locale_context.culture: NHS information-governance culture: security- and data-protection-led (UK GDPR, DSPT, Caldicott-style confidentiality), aligning with the UK government's outcome-based, pro-innovation AI assurance guidance rather than AI-specific law.

key_dates.event: Approved by the Trust Risk & Assurance Committee (TRAC); effective from June 2024

versions.title: Version 1 (effective June 2024)
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: third parties accessing Trust information systems
directors, heads of department and line managers
covered_systems: AI-enabled tools (e.g. Microsoft PowerApps, security tooling, chatbots)
NLP, computer vision, neural networks and distributed AI
covered_activities: development of AI solutions (including proofs of concept)
staff use of LLMs and public AI tools
integration of AI with Trust systems
exceptions: robotic process automation (out of scope as AI, though IG and security policies still apply)
AI as a medical device governed by the Trust Medical Device Policy
research aspects governed by the Trust R&D policy
conditions: sensitive/highly sensitive/restricted data may be used in AI only if wholly owned by the Trust with contractual clauses; exceptions signed off by IG, IS and the IAO
personal-use LLM registration with a work email only after DPIA approval for a documented use case
objective: Embed information security and information governance in any use of AI at the Trust, protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of Trust data and assets and supporting future Trust AI policies.
principles: security by design in procurement and development
parent_policy: Trust Information Security Policy Framework and Information Governance Policy

related_policies.policy: Introduction to AI Assurance (UK Government guidance, February 2024)
UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
GSTT Information Security Policy; Information Governance Policy; Third Party Security Policy; Personal Device (BYOD) policy

conflict_rule: Sits within the Trust Information Security Policy Framework and Information Governance Policy; all Trust policies and standards apply to AI solutions. AI as a medical device is governed by the Trust Medical Device Policy and research by the R&D policy (s.3.2).

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/guy-nhs.pdf). (asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper commit b8ac8876beec6593ef5685d7d7e64cc94f9cc55b.) The asago PDF has 9 pages while the footer reads 'Page x of 13': Appendices A and B (risk assessment and countermeasures) are not in this copy, so they are not reflected here. Version 1, effective June 2024 (exact day not stated); 'Approved by: TRAC June 2024' and final draft dated 15/04/2024. Section numbering in the source skips 6 and has two sections numbered 8. No official public URL is printed (only an intranet GTi link), so the asago copy is the source_uri. Not verified whether a later version has replaced it. Binding=false: not law, but mandatory internally for Trust staff, contractors and third parties accessing Trust systems; inputting sensitive data into public AI tools without approval is treated as a data breach (s.5.6.2).

clauses.original_text: Under no circumstances should personal identifiable or business sensitive information be entered in to the LLM. Only information that is already available in the public domain should be used. Unless data access and sharing can be appropriately restricted.
clauses.object: personal identifiable or business sensitive information
clauses.requirement: only public-domain information may be entered into LLMs unless access and sharing can be restricted
clauses.exception: where data access and sharing can be appropriately restricted (s.8: guaranteed via contractual clauses)
clauses.purpose: prevent disclosure of patient, staff and business data to LLM providers
clauses.affected_asset: patient and staff personal data; Trust business-sensitive information
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs and publicly available AI tools used by Trust staff
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed. Worded 'should' but 'under no circumstances' makes it a prohibition; repeated in s.8 Do's and Don'ts with examples (patient/staff information, IP, proprietary code, passwords, keys, card numbers).

clauses.original_text: LLMs should not be used to make medical diagnoses or to provide medical advice if not approved for use as medical device.
clauses.action: use LLMs for diagnosis or medical advice
clauses.object: LLMs not approved as medical devices
clauses.requirement: no medical diagnosis or advice from LLMs unless approved as a medical device
clauses.condition: unless the LLM is approved for use as a medical device
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs not approved as medical devices
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed.

clauses.original_text: LLMs should be used with caution, and their output should always be verified via human intervention.
clauses.requirement: human verification of all LLM output
clauses.purpose: avoid reliance on incorrect or misleading output
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy of Trust information and clinical safety
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs and publicly available AI tools used by Trust staff
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed. s.8 restates it as 'LLM output must always be verified via human intervention' and asks staff to fact-check all content against trusted sources.

clauses.original_text: Biometric data for user logins/identification (as defined by UK GDPR Article 4.14) must not be used for any AI technology within Trust-owned solutions.
clauses.requirement: no biometric authentication/identification in Trust-owned AI solutions
clauses.exception: personal devices (refer to the Personal Device (BYOD) policy)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed. Personal devices are dealt with under the BYOD policy.

clauses.original_text: AI tooling must never be used to circumvent security controls at the Trust. (For example hacking devices, jailbreak, eavesdropping, etc).
clauses.requirement: AI tools must not be used for hacking, jailbreaking, eavesdropping or other circumvention of controls
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed.

clauses.original_text: Trust Policy applies. Data breaches involving any AI tool, including Trust developed and third party solutions, must be reported promptly via the Trust Incident Management reporting system (RADAR).
clauses.object: data breaches involving any AI tool
clauses.recipient: Information Governance and Information Security teams
clauses.requirement: prompt incident reporting of AI-related data breaches
clauses.purpose: timely incident management and notification to IG and IS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago copy of the Trust PDF (pdftotext -layout); line breaks collapsed. s.5.6.2 adds that inputting sensitive or proprietary data into public AI tools without IG/IS approval is considered a data breach.
